name: Bhakra Nangal Dam
reservoirName: Gobind Sagar (named after 10th Sikh Guru Gobind Singh)
examFacts: Second tallest dam in India (226 m) after Tehri Dam (260.5 m).
Jawaharlal Nehru famously described Bhakra Dam as the 'Temple of Resurgent India' during its dedication in 1963.
Nangal Dam is a barrage located 13 km downstream of Bhakra Dam to divert water into the Nangal Hydel Channel and Bhakra Main Line canal.
Irrigates over 10 million acres across Punjab, Haryana, and Rajasthan, forming the bedrock of the Green Revolution.
Operated by the Bhakra Beas Management Board (BBMB).

name: Tehri Dam
examFacts: Tallest dam in India and the 12th tallest dam in the world, rising 260.5 meters high.
Features an underground powerhouse and a pumped-storage plant (PSP) with an ultimate installed capacity of 2,400 MW.
Subject of the famous Anti-Tehri Dam Movement led by environmentalist Sunderlal Bahuguna concerning seismic hazards (situated in Central Himalayan Seismic Gap Zone V).
Provides vital municipal drinking water to New Delhi (~300 cusecs) and urban centres of Uttar Pradesh.
Koteshwar Dam is the re-regulating dam built 22 km downstream on the Bhagirathi.

name: Hirakud Dam
type: Composite Earth, Concrete and Masonry Dam
examFacts: One of the longest earthen dams in the world: main section is 4.8 km long, flanked by earthen dykes giving a total length of 25.8 km.
Inaugurated by Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru in January 1957 as one of the first major river valley projects post-independence.
Substantially tamed the recurrent catastrophic monsoon floods of the Mahanadi delta in coastal Odisha.
Hirakud Reservoir was designated as a Ramsar Wetland of International Importance in 2021.
Features two observation towers: Gandhi Minar at the southern end and Nehru Minar at the northern end.

name: Sardar Sarovar Dam
examFacts: Centerpiece of the 30-dam Narmada Valley Project, distributing water across Gujarat, Rajasthan, and Madhya Pradesh.
Narmada Main Canal taking off from the dam is the world's largest irrigation canal by capacity (40,000 cusecs), extending 458 km to the Rajasthan border.
Center of the Narmada Bachao Andolan (NBA) led by Medha Patkar and Baba Amte over rehabilitation and environmental impacts.
Statue of Unity, the world's tallest statue (182 m), stands on Sadhu Bet island facing the dam.
Power generated is shared among Madhya Pradesh (57%), Maharashtra (27%), and Gujarat (16%).

name: Nagarjuna Sagar Dam
examFacts: One of the earliest and largest masonry dams built in the world, completed in 1967.
Named after the 2nd-century CE Buddhist philosopher Acharya Nagarjuna who founded Madhyamaka philosophy.
Nagarjunakonda, an ancient Buddhist settlement in the reservoir basin, was excavated and preserved on an island museum within the reservoir.
Left canal is named Lal Bahadur Shastri Canal (Telangana) and Right canal is named Jawahar Canal (Andhra Pradesh).
Forms the northern boundary of the Nagarjunsagar-Srisailam Tiger Reserve, India's largest tiger reserve.

name: Idukki Dam
type: Double-curvature Parabolic Thin Concrete Arch Dam
examFacts: One of the highest arch dams in Asia and the only double-curvature arch dam in India, standing 168.9 meters high between Kuravan and Kurathi hills.
Constructed with financial and technical assistance from the Government of Canada (SNC-Lavalin).
Operated with two associated dams: Cheruthoni (concrete gravity dam) and Kulamavu (masonry gravity dam), which together impound the reservoir.
Moolamattom Underground Powerhouse is the largest underground hydroelectric power station in Kerala.
Idukki Wildlife Sanctuary surrounds the reservoir, protecting Asian elephants, sambar, and gaur.
